per_window.ps-ns: no_evidence_in_window for large-amplitude motion, protein average only: native free enzyme average S2 0.868 ± 0.042 at 300 K in MES (J10, r28) and 0.910 ± 0.051 in an abstract that calls the backbone rigid (J11, r48, indirect); residue-level S2 was not read, so local flexible loops are not excluded. Guanidine lowers average S2 to 0.831 and TMAO restores 0.858 (J21); pTppAp binding raises S2 (J22, abstract).
per_window.us-ms: dynamic_in_window for free WT in low-salt MES at pH 6.3-6.4. Global fits: 1,080 / 1,390 / 1,750 s-1 at 10 / 20 / 25 °C with a 90-93% major state (J1, r1-r3); about 1,700 s-1 with 5% minor state (J3, r24); 1,621 ± 152 s-1 (J8, s17). Cluster fits separate a loop 1/beta1/beta4 network around His48 (1,100-2,650 s-1 at pH 6.4, 980-1,970 s-1 at pH 7.0, 10-25 °C; at pH 4.5 too fast for CPMG, 13,400 s-1 by R1rho; J5), loop 4 (A64, K66, T70, N71; 508-1,610 s-1, pH-independent 5.5-7.0; J6) and Arg33 (1,215 s-1 at 25 °C, pA 99.5%; J7); the His48 network carries a solvent isotope effect of 2.2 and loop 4 none (J3, J4). Exchange persists with pTppAp, 5'-AMP and 3'-UMP bound (J16, J17). His48-network mutants T17A and H48C-4MI keep exchange while H48C, H48G, T82A and the loop-1 chimera lose it there; loop 4 exchange survives those mutations and speeds up in A109G (J23, J24, inference_from_mutant). Phosphate, sulfate and acetate change residue-specific dispersion (J19, artefact_suspected). Ligand release rates (J18, J25) are binding kinetics and are not counted.
per_window.slower_than_ms: not_measured for the free native enzyme (J12): no CEST, ZZ-exchange or backbone HDX rate in the rows. pTppAp release at 30 (288 K) and 80 s-1 (298 K) is binding kinetics (r7, r8).
per_window.undetermined: His48 slow pH-linked transition and its exchange broadening in chloride, removed by acetate (J13, r52, r62, abstracts); proteolysis of the 15-23 hinge loop (J14); free-enzyme crystal alternates of His119 and Gln11, temperature- and humidity-dependent loop and hinge movement (J15, structure_only); ligand, anion, pH and mutant crystal alternates (J26, structure_only); restrained and unrestrained MD (J27, md_only). Not judged: His C2 H/D exchange (r32, r33), gas-phase ion mobility (r42-r44), acid denaturation, thermal unfolding and stability (r51, r56, r57), binding thermodynamics and volumetry (r53, r61), probe-labelled FRET and EPR constructs (r66, r67), the 288 K pTppAp line-shape row (r7).

protein_summary.wt_apo_answer: Yes: in low-salt MES at pH 6.3-6.4, free wild-type RNase A exchanges on the microsecond-millisecond scale in a loop 1/beta1/beta4 network around His48 (S15, S16, T17, F46, T82, D83, Q101; kex 2,650 s-1 at 25 °C and pH 6.4, 1,100 s-1 at 10 °C, minor state about 7.5%) and in loop 4 near His119 (A64, K66, T70, N71; kex 1,610 s-1 at 25 °C down to 508 s-1 at 10 °C, minor state about 4% pooled across pH), single global fits give 1,750 ± 130 s-1 at 25 °C, 1,390 ± 70 s-1 at 20 °C (the RelaxDB label condition) and 1,080 ± 80 s-1 at 10 °C (pH 6.3, minor state 7-10%), and Arg33 exchanges separately at 1,215 s-1 at 25 °C with a 0.5% minor state, its dispersion flattening at 15 and 10 °C.
open_conflicts: Number of processes: Beach 2005 (r1-r3), Cole 2002 (r47) and Kovrigin 2006 (s1-s4, 'identical behavior is observed for all exchanging residues') fit one global process, while Watt 2007 (r24-r27) finds an isotope-sensitive His48 network and an isotope-insensitive loop 4 region, and JPCB 2015 (r14-r19, r68) separates cluster 1, cluster 2 and R33 with different pH and temperature dependence. All agree exchange exists; they disagree on whether it is one collective motion.

Cluster labels are reversed between papers: 'cluster 1' is the loop 1/His48 network in Watt 2007, Doucet 2011 and JPCB 2015, but loop 4 in Gagne 2015 (s17-s22). Rows cannot be pooled by cluster number.
Anion samples: whether the dispersion changes in phosphate, sulfate and acetate (J19) are altered intramolecular motion or free/anion-bound exchange is unresolved by the authors themselves.
questions_for_gina: The RelaxDB curator note says the labels are residues with Rex > 3 Hz at 20 °C in 500 or 600 MHz data, recreating Beach 2005 Fig. 4B (43 residues, membership shown only in the figure), but only 13 of them entered the 1,390 s-1 global fit (r2). Should the atlas treat all 43 threshold residues as exchange-positive, and which label set is current (Hugging Face and the metadata sheet differ at 4 RNase positions; accession P61824 vs bovine P61823)?

Every free-WT CPMG sample in the rows is in 5-20 mM MES with 7-10 mM NaCl (the 2013-2015 samples also carry 1% w/v DSS, a sulfonate), and the only control, MES versus unbuffered at pH 6.4, is stated as 'identical ms motions' without data. Is that enough to treat MES/DSS as inert for RNase A, given that phosphate, sulfate and acetate visibly change the dispersion?
protein_summary.buffer_note: Untested condition for the key apo data: free-WT CPMG was recorded in 20 mM perdeuterated MES pH 6.3 with 10 mM NaCl (Beach 2005, r1-r3) or 5 mM MES-NaOH pH 6.4 with 7 mM NaCl, 0.01% NaN3 and, in the 2013-2015 papers, 1% w/v DSS (r10, r14-r19, r68, s17); Watt 2007 and Kovrigin 2006 buffers are not in the main text. No apo WT CPMG row used phosphate. The buffer paper states MES and unbuffered samples at pH 6.4 gave identical ms motions but shows no data (indirect), and shows that 100 mM phosphate, 80 mM sulfate and 100 mM acetate, which bind at or near the active site, remove dispersion at Ala4 and change rates at loop 4 and Ala109, with sulfate adding dispersion near loop 1 and Asp83; in acetate Lys66 is not determined (ND) while A64, T70, N71 and A109 keep fitted rates (J19). Any RNase A dispersion in these anions, in high-sulfate crystals, or in acetate-based His C2 exchange and ion-mobility samples carries this caveat; the effect of DSS was not tested. Recurring caveat: the buffer paper prints Rex ratios with a unit (s-1); this file writes them as bare ratios.
